items.head: 8ede68574392af1cf9123a4aec179b5557689964
items.title: Report incomplete packet evidence after capture and inventory limits (R3.12)
items.body:
## Why

Packet tools could report complete evidence after a capture reader warning or a real scan/inventory limit. Their coverage described only the retained page, so a caller could mistake an omitted packet, flow or address for a confirmed absence.

For example, a capture containing 5,001 packets and 10,002 distinct IP addresses retains the first 10,000 addresses. Requesting all 10,000 retained inventory rows previously returned complete coverage.

## Changes

- Carry capture warnings and scan/flow limits into `packets_capture_show` and `packets_fields_show` coverage. Preserve readable packets, retained flow pages and continuation offsets.
- Keep exact packet totals when only inventory rows or distinct values are limited. Omit an exact coverage total when the capture scan is incomplete, and qualify flow-filter results when flow identifiers were omitted.
- Expose `truncated`, `capped_inventories`, `rows_limited` and capture warnings in inventory evidence, with an explicit limitation for the built-in packet scan budget.
- Track distinct-value limits in the tshark field aggregator while continuing to count already retained values. When the existing 64 MiB stdout cap cuts a TSV record, retain only complete records; a partial field does not become an address or request.

Warnings are handled conservatively without matching their English wording. The observed packet counts remain available even when coverage cannot assert an exact complete total.

## Validation

- [Original/fixed regression run](https://github.com/Afloat16/billion-context/actions/runs/43055226582): original `adeddc9` fails 10 cases and passes the 3 complete-input/exact-boundary controls; the fixed code passes all 13. These include the real 5,000,000-record scan, 100,000-flow and 10,000-value budgets, plus an actual 64 MiB process-output cap.
- [Native file comparison](https://github.com/Afloat16/billion-context/actions/runs/43056191802): official libpcap 1.10.5 at `bbcbc9174df3298a854daee2b3e666a4b6e5383a` writes classic captures and independently reads classic and generated pcapng fixtures. Eight files check every packet's bytes, lengths, timestamp and link type, including 10,002-endpoint captures, damaged readable prefixes and empty controls. The actual engine tests fail 3 cases and pass 2 controls on the original code; all 5 pass with the fix.
- [Latest parser integration](https://github.com/Afloat16/billion-context/actions/runs/43058913342) at `46c531c`, based on `0634265`: full engine/formats/testkit suites pass **2,399 tests, 0 failures, 17 existing ignored tests**. Formatting, strict all-target Clippy, layers, locks, secrets and the complete five-crate WebAssembly gate pass.
- [Final source/dependency verification](https://github.com/Afloat16/billion-context/actions/runs/43059889897) checks final `8ede685` on `86d047c`. The packet implementation, regressions and entire lower-layer tree match the fully tested integration. The five newly merged upstream AI files are inherited exactly; dependency manifests and the lockfile are identical. Formatting and repository contracts are checked again.

The process tests emit actual TSV streams through the normal external-process path, including an exact 64 MiB control and a stream that ends inside a record at the cap. They use a controlled local producer. The independent native file checks use fixed official libpcap source; they do not claim that a real tshark binary ran.

The original [native package setup attempt](https://github.com/Afloat16/billion-context/actions/runs/43054523894) passed formatting, then failed to resolve Ubuntu's archive host before any product tests ran. That red run is retained. Native validation was moved to a file-only libpcap build without APT dependencies.
items.scope: Propagate capture, flow and inventory incompleteness through all three packet evidence tools; do not count incomplete tshark TSV records after the existing stdout cap.

dedupe.rejected_candidate: pcapng if_tsoffset already merged in #397; timestamp/record budget corrections already merged in #1091

native.native_build: Official fixed libpcap source; file-only PCAP_TYPE=null; runner-preinstalled build dependencies; no APT installation
native.comparison: Every packet's bytes, captured/original length, timestamp and link type; empty, complete, 10,002-endpoint inventory and damaged readable-prefix controls in classic pcap and pcapng.
native.external_process_scope: Controlled native child emits actual TSV streams through the production process runner, including exact and truncated 64 MiB cases.

retained_failures.reason: Official signed Ubuntu package setup could not resolve archive.ubuntu.com. Native fixtures, regressions and remaining gates did not run.

Validation-only identity harness used git rev-parse at a shallow parent boundary. No product failure; later gates were skipped. Replaced ancestry traversal with parsing raw commit parent headers; corrected run 43057974492 passed.

limitations: Capture warnings conservatively prevent complete coverage without matching English warning text.
Observed packet counts remain in results even when exact complete coverage totals are unavailable.
No live packet capture or real tshark binary was run.
Original parser behavior, packet/inventory budgets and API parameters are unchanged.
